test_harness_notes: SBA-011 and SBA-025 are NEGATIVE TESTS. The harness MUST assert that the error/violation fires. A clean result is a test FAILURE for both.

test_cases.name: Abbreviation Lexicon — Mid-Sentence Suppression with Correct Terminal Boundary
test_cases.goal: Verify that an abbreviation in the lexicon is suppressed mid-sentence while the correct sentence-terminal period still triggers Rule B-1. Tests that lexicon suppression does not prevent legitimate boundaries.
test_cases.input: The Delegation met at No. 15 Main Street. CMS reviewed the report.
test_cases.tokenization_note: Assumes 'No.' is tokenized as a single token per spaCy-compatible rules. If the implementation tokenizes 'No.' as ['No', '.'], the lexicon MUST store both forms or normalize tokens before lookup. EDGE CASE — DOCUMENTED: A sentence ending in 'Vote No.' should still trigger a boundary, because 'No.' in this terminal position functions as a sentence-ending word rather than a mid-clause abbreviation. The segmenter will eventually need a heuristic that detects when an abbreviation occupies an absolute clause-terminal position and is followed by an uppercase token — in that case, the boundary should fire even if the token is in the lexicon. This heuristic is not in scope for Wave 1 but should be added to the Wave 2 backlog.

expected_behavior.segmenter: 'No.' suppressed (in lexicon). Rule B-1 fires at the standalone '.' after 'Street' — followed by uppercase 'CMS', preceding span contains finite verb 'met'.
expected_behavior.metadata: sentences.length === 2. sentences[0] contains 'No. 15 Main Street'. sentences[1] starts with 'CMS'.

success_criteria: sentences.length === 2 (not 3, which would indicate a false split at 'No.').

test_cases.invocation_protocol: Call buildGraph() independently for each input with separate parsingActIds and ibeIris. Tier 2 IRI for 'CMS' must be string-identical across both.

expected_behavior.both_invocations: Both produce a Tier 2 node for 'CMS'. Both Tier 2 IRIs are identical strings. Neither IRI contains the parsingActId, a UUID, or any timestamp.
expected_behavior.failure_mode: If the IRI contains the parsingActId or any randomness, the document service cannot merge graphs by entity — cross-input identity is broken.

success_criteria: Neither Tier 2 IRI contains the string value of parsingActId from invocation_1.
Neither Tier 2 IRI contains the string value of parsingActId from invocation_2.
Running the test three times in sequence produces the same IRI all three times.
FAILURE MODE: IRI containing 'uuid', a timestamp, or a parsingActId requires removing parse-time randomness before corpus migration proceeds.

test_cases.name: TokenSpanCardinalityError — Projection Integrity Guard
test_cases.expected_phase: JSON-to-RDF Projection (§4.6.6) — before SHACL validation executes
test_cases.goal: Verify that the JSON-to-RDF Projection detects and rejects a SentenceRecord where tokenSpan implies a different token count than the tokens array actually contains. Structural companion to the Poison Pill (SBA-011): SBA-011 guards arc locality; SBA-025 guards span cardinality.
test_cases.input: INJECTED_FIXTURE — inject the fixture below directly into the JSON-to-RDF Projection. Do not use text parsing.

injected_fixture.cardinality_note: tokenSpan: [0, 5] implies 5 - 0 + 1 = 6 tokens. tokens.length === 3. Mismatch: 6 ≠ 3. The projection MUST throw TokenSpanCardinalityError rather than silently emitting tagteam:tokenCount with a wrong value, which would cause SBA_ForestStructureShape to use 6 as the bounds-check denominator against a sentence that actually has 3 tokens.

success_criteria: TokenSpanCardinalityError is thrown during the JSON-to-RDF Projection phase.
The error is thrown BEFORE any SHACL shapes execute.
Error message specifies: tokenSpan [0, 5] implies 6 tokens, but tokens.length === 3.
No partial RDF output is emitted for the malformed SentenceRecord.
TEST PASSES ONLY WHEN THE ERROR IS THROWN. Successful projection without error is a test FAILURE.
